title: Two Sum
statement:
Given a list of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target, as a list [i, j] with i < j.

Exactly one pair adds up to target, and you may not use the same element twice.
hints: A brute-force check of every pair works. Can you avoid the inner loop?
For each number x, the number you need is target - x. How could you find out quickly whether you've already seen it?
Keep a dictionary from value to index while you scan. Before storing x, check whether target - x is already in it.
expected_complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space with a hash map (O(n^2) time, O(1) space for brute force)

title: Valid Parentheses
statement: Given a string s containing only the characters ()[]{}, return True if the brackets are balanced: every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, in the correct order. An empty string is balanced.
hints: The most recently opened bracket must be the first one closed. Which data structure gives you 'last in, first out'?
Push opening brackets onto a stack. When you see a closing bracket, what must be on top of the stack?
Map each closing bracket to its opening one. Fail if the stack is empty or the top doesn't match, and check the stack is empty at the end.
expected_complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the stack

title: Valid Palindrome
statement: Return True if the string s reads the same forwards and backwards after converting all letters to lower case and removing every character that is not a letter or a digit.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hints: First think about which characters you need to compare, and how to ignore the rest.
Instead of building a cleaned copy, you can use two pointers, one at each end, moving towards each other.
Skip characters that are not alphanumeric on each side, compare the lower-case characters, and stop when the pointers meet.
expected_complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space with two pointers

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring (a contiguous run of characters) that contains no repeated character.
hints: Checking every substring works but is slow. Think about a window that only grows and shrinks.
Keep a window [left, right] with no repeats. When s[right] is already inside the window, move left past its previous position.
Store the last index of each character. When you see a repeat inside the window, set left = last[ch] + 1, and track the best right - left + 1.
expected_complexity: O(n) time and O(k) space, where k is the number of distinct characters

title: Merge Intervals
statement: Given a list of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the result sorted by start. Intervals that touch, such as [1, 4] and [4, 5], count as overlapping.
hints: Overlaps are much easier to spot if the intervals are in some order. Which order?
After sorting by start, an interval overlaps the previous merged one exactly when its start is <= that one's end.
Sort by start, then walk the list: either extend the last merged interval's end with max(), or append a new interval.
expected_complexity: O(n log n) time for the sort and O(n) space for the output

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: Given a list of integers nums, return a list answer where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. Do it without using division.
hints: answer[i] is (product of everything to the left of i) times (product of everything to the right of i).
You can compute all the left products in one pass from the start, and all the right products in one pass from the end.
Fill answer with left products first, then walk backwards keeping a running right product and multiply it in. That needs O(1) extra space.
reference_solution:
def product_except_self(nums):
    answer = [1] * len(nums)
    left = 1
    for i in range(len(nums)):
        answer[i] = left
        left *= nums[i]
    right = 1
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        answer[i] *= right
        right *= nums[i]
    return answer
expected_complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space (not counting the output)

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Given a list of non-negative integers heights, where each value is the height of a bar of width 1, return how many units of rain water are trapped between the bars after it rains.
hints: The water above bar i is min(tallest bar to its left, tallest bar to its right) - heights[i], if that is positive.
You could precompute the tallest bar to the left and to the right of every position with two passes. Can you avoid the extra arrays?
Use two pointers from both ends with running left_max and right_max. Always move the side with the smaller max: its water level is already known.
expected_complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space with two pointers (O(n) space with prefix/suffix max arrays)
